page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-112 is a compute-focused server instance featuring 112 vCPUs and 448 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 56 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the c2d-standard-112 demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring 164277.47 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 94624.64 in Passmark CPU testing. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 7743.53 GB/sec and uncached large-block read speeds at 273.18 GB/sec. Cryptographic and physics simulations perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 131032.1 and a physics score of 17801.37. Ray tracing benchmarks also place in the top tier.

While multi-threaded operations and raw compute throughput are strong, single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1666.0 and average single-threaded gzip compression. Large-model LLM text generation represents a performance bottleneck, with the 70B model achieving only 2.74 tokens/sec. The instance is highly cost-efficient for dense multi-core workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, database operations, software compilation, and parallelized physics simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-112 is a compute-focused instance featuring 112 vCPUs and 448 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 56 physical cores, it delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth, reaching 7743.53 GB/sec for cached reads. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, making it a specialized choice for compute-heavy, memory-stable workloads. Benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in database operations, software compilation, and ray tracing, though single-core execution and large-model LLM text generation are moderate. It is best suited for parallelized workloads, static web serving, and high-throughput computational tasks.
